title: Rio Ngumoha made Liverpool play better. Arne Slot now has a decision to make
content:
Arne Slot was adamant that there was not much difference performance wise from Liverpool’s previous trip to Molineux three days earlier.

“Every stat is almost identical,” he said. “Overall, there were a lot of similarities. They scored tonight from their only chance. The other night they only created one chance and scored twice.”

The Dutch head coach had a point when you crunch the headline numbers. Liverpool cruised into the quarter-finals of the FA Cup with a comfortable 3-1 victory on Friday after having 20 shots versus four, nine on target versus three, and creating an expected goals (xG) of 1.8 versus 0.44.

In midweek at the same stadium, the champions had slumped to an embarrassing 2-1 defeat in the Premier League against its last-placed side — despite having 20 shots to four, seven on target to three, and compiling an xG of 2.56 versus 0.44.

Yet avenging that setback was not simply about being more ruthless at one end and less careless at the other.  The biggest distinction between the two displays came in the form of an exciting young winger who tormented Wolverhampton Wanderers’ back line last night.

Handed just his fourth start of the season in all competitions, Rio Ngumoha gave Liverpool something they had been missing. A lack of pace in wide areas has repeatedly hurt Slot’s side during this campaign but the teenager’s presence on the left flank turbo-charged them.

Quick, direct, skilful and fearless, Ngumoha set the tone as he provided Liverpool with the kind of outlet they did not possess in the midweek defeat. Even during a goalless first half, they looked like a different beast against the hosts’ stubborn defensive set-up with the England Under-19s international repeatedly skipping past Jackson Tchatchoua.

After Andy Robertson’s sweet strike broke the deadlock early in the second half, Ngumoha was heavily involved in the move for the second goal as he picked out the Scottish left-back on the overlap. Robertson’s low cross was turned in by Mohamed Salah, who could celebrate his 254th goal for the club after a lengthy VAR check.

Ngumoha, who had made a lively cameo off the bench on Tuesday, received a richly deserved standing ovation from the away end and a warm embrace from Slot when he was replaced by the returning Florian Wirtz in the 69th minute.

The youngster completed more dribbles (three), won the most duels (six), had the most shots on target (two) and had more touches in the opposition box (nine) than any of his team-mates. He created one chance and completed 30 of his 33 passes (91 per cent). Not bad for the first senior start of his career away from Anfield.

“It is special if you are 17 and you play in a FA Cup match between two Premier League teams,” Slot said.

“If you are then able to impact it with some very good one v one situations — that’s what makes him special. There are not many players in modern football who can take one v ones on but he can.

“He did better than three days ago because he kept the ball more. Three days ago he lost it a few times. Defensively, he didn’t have to do as much, facing five defenders, so he could use all his energy for attacking.”

In the build up to Friday’s tie, Slot had delivered a defence of senior wingers Cody Gakpo and Salah, insisting it’s “the hardest position to play in current football…because there are limited spaces and the players you face are so good”.

However, the slump in their output is stark. In early March last season they had 46 goals between them in all competitions, this time around they boast 17. Both have looked too predictable and unable to really stretch defences.

With Ngumoha starting on the left and Gakpo shifted into the middle with top scorer Hugo Ekitike was rested with one eye on Tuesday’s Champions League round of 16 first leg away to Galatasaray, Liverpool’s attack benefited from an injection of greater energy and dynamism. Playing left wing did not look anything like as hard as the teenager dazzled with his footwork.

It is becoming increasingly clear why the Anfield hierarchy regarded it as a coup and Chelsea were so aggrieved when Ngumoha decided to move north to Merseyside in the summer of 2024. He felt the pathway to the first team was clearer so it has proved.

Last month’s ruling by a tribunal that Liverpool must pay Chelsea £2.8 million in compensation, potentially rising to £6.8m over the coming years, feels like small change.

There has been a clamour among the fanbase for Slot to play Ngumoha more regularly. At times he has been left on the bench too long when Liverpool have been crying out for inspiration.

His age and the need to protect him does have to be factored in. He has clocked up more appearances (18) and starts (four) in all competitions than any other 17-year-old at a Premier League club this season. His attitude and application, as well as his talent, has endeared him to the senior professionals in the squad.

“Rio is only young but his decision making was outstanding. He’s so good for 17,” Robertson told TNT Sports. “Sometimes he wants to take the whole team on and it’s not the right time, but he made pretty much every right decision. He works so hard and listens to all the experienced lads.

“Tonight, he really came of age. If he puts in more performances like that he will get more and more game time. He’s got quick feet, he’s not scared to take anyone on. We keep going on at him about decision making as that’s what’s going to make him a top player.

“He’s got everything in his toolbox to go and have such a special career. If we can help him on the way then so be it.”

After Ngumoha was replaced, Curtis Jones added a classy third before Hwang Hee Chan’s late consolation.

Wolves head coach Rob Edwards certainly saw something different compared to three days earlier. “Liverpool are a bit good, aren’t they? I thought we saw the best version of them tonight,” he said.  “It was really difficult to put a dent on them. They were at a really high level.”

It was Ngumoha who provided the X-factor.
